items.title: gfx host on X11: give the GPU surface its own X connection, so no driver thread reads winit's (the root-cause fix behind F169's wake schedule)
items.kind: design question (native runtime; needs `unsafe`) — OWNER RULING
items.discussion: raised by lane f169-58 (Order 58, 2026-11-12); F169's fix is a bounded wake schedule after each present, which removes the measured loss but leaves a present stalled past about 2 s uncovered and costs up to eight wakes after the last frame
items.area: crates/vilan-rt-gfx/src/host (surface creation), wgpu's raw-handle surface target
items.body: winit and wgpu share one X connection today because the surface is made from the window. A second connection opened for the surface alone would keep Mesa's swapchain thread off winit's socket, and the wake schedule could go. It needs raw window and display handles (`unsafe`), which `vilan-rt-gfx` forbids by lint. QUESTION for the owner: allow one audited `unsafe` block in the gfx crate for this, or keep the schedule. Integrator's recommendation: keep the schedule until a real-GPU run shows a loss it does not cover; the schedule is cheap, proven by 200 runs, and platform-neutral in its failure mode. Also unknown: NVIDIA's driver; Mesa hardware drivers likely share the defect (Present events read on their swapchain threads) and are covered by the schedule.

items.title: `dial_cancel`'s hung-dial pins assert that the client's upgrade arrived before the cancel, which a loaded Windows runner does not guarantee
items.discussion: CI run 43260260833 (next 9b39ddbc), windows 3/4: `dial_within_times_out_a_hung_dial_and_closes_its_socket` read nothing before the close; the `within` pin was relaxed to `upgrade or nothing` at next 14a98c85 (CI green)
items.body: The 300 ms deadline is the program's own clock and the listener's backlog completes the connection before the client writes, so the cancel can beat the first write. Cause not proven from the log (an abortive close discarding unread data would look the same). The `within` pin on node is relaxed; the `service` (explicit cancel) pins and the native legs still assert the upgrade and have the same shape. If one of them flakes, relax it the same way or have the program print a line once the socket has written, and wait on that. Low priority; close at the sweep if no further flake.
